violations.text: Chicken stock, and marinera sauce, which was previously cooked and cooled, was not reheated for hot holding. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food that is cooked, cooled, and reheated for hot holding must be reheated to 165 degrees Fahrenheit or above for 15 seconds. Chicken stock, and sauce was reheated to above 165 DF at the time of inspection. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 06/15/2026

The presence of mice is not controlled as evidenced by droppings along floor of basement and behind equipment in the kitchen. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests must be controlled by routinely inspecting the premises for evidence of pests, using acceptable methods to control pests, eliminating harborage conditions, and routinely inspecting incoming shipments of food and supplies. Establishment is to clean any and all droppings using appropriate means of sanitization to monitor for new activity. Establishment is to continue to work with pest control, and increase pest control as frequently as needed. New Violation. Correct By: 06/15/2026

Wood is used in the construction of support beam in the bar area. Non-food contact surfaces of equipment that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other food soiling or that require frequent cleaning must be constructed of a nonabsorbent and smooth material. Per PIC, the beam at the bar will be sealed. Repeat Violation. Correct By: 06/15/2026
The wall in the walk-in cooler area is in poor repair. The physical facilities must be maintained in good repair. New Violation. Correct By: 06/23/2026

Food contact surfaces of equipment/utensils ice machine, slicer, and can opener were observed with an accumulation of food and debris. The food contact surfaces of equipment must be clean to sight and touch. Ice machine was emptied and turned off at the time of inspection. Can opener was moved to ware-washing area, and slicer was cleaned and sanitized at the time of inspection. Establishment is not to use ice machine until it is properly cleaned and sanitized. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 06/02/2026

The quaternary ammonium concentration in the sanitizing solution of the 3-bay sink was observed exceeding 400 parts per million (ppm). According to the manufacturer's use directions, the concentration of the quaternary ammonium must be 200-300 ppm. Establishment is to have sanitizer dispenser serviced. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 06/02/2026

Various food in the walk-in cooler was observed not marked with the date of preparation. Ready-to-eat time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods prepared in the establishment and held for more than 24 hours must be marked with the date of preparation. New Violation. Correct By: 06/02/2026

Proper cooling methods were not used for time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods. Mashed potatoes were observed cooling on counter covered in containers greater than four inches deep. Mashed potatoes were put on to sheet pan and placed into walk-in cooler at the time of inspection. Proper cooling methods reviewed with PIC. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 06/02/2026

The presence of mice is not controlled as evidenced by droppings along floor of kitchen and basement. The presence of insects, rodents, and other pests must be controlled by routinely inspecting the premises for evidence of pests, using acceptable methods to control pests, eliminating harborage conditions, and routinely inspecting incoming shipments of food and supplies. Establishment is to clean any and all droppings using appropriate means of sanitization. Establishment is to continue to work with pest control and have a pest control report available for inspector at the time of next inspection. New Violation. Correct By: 06/02/2026

Wood is used in the construction of part of the walk-in cooler wall and the bar area. Non-food contact surfaces of equipment that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other food soiling or that require frequent cleaning must be constructed of a nonabsorbent and smooth material. New Violation. Correct By: 06/02/2026
The facility is lacking test strips to measure the concentration of the quat sanitizing solution for the 3-bay sink. Establishment is to obtain test strips. New Violation. Correct By: 06/05/2026

The non-food contact surfaces of the walk-in cooler fans have an accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned to sight and touch. New Violation. Correct By: 06/02/2026
The outside grease bin was observed with an accumulation of debris. Outside refuse areas must be maintained. New Violation. Correct By: 06/02/2026

The floors and walls throughout the facility have an accumulation of soil residue and/or food debris. The physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. New Violation. Correct By: 06/02/2026
The wall in the walk-in cooler area, and floor to the left of hand sink in kitchen is in poor repair. The physical facilities must be maintained in good repair. New Violation. Correct By: 06/23/2026

The establishment does not employ a full-time, on-site manager certified in food safety at all times when time temperature control for safety (TCS) food is being prepared, handled, and/or served. New Violation. Correct By: 03/06/2024
The establishment does not have a written procedure for cleaning vomit and diarrhea. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 03/06/2024

Shellfish tags must be maintained for 90 days in chronological order and the date when the last shellfish was used from the bag must be noted on the shellfish tag. New Violation. Correct By: 03/06/2024

Raw animal foods (fish) were observed stored above ready-to-eat foods (pasta) in the walk-in refrigerator. Raw animal foods must be separated from raw ready-to-eat food such as vegetables during storage. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 03/06/2024

Food contact surfaces of equipment/utensils (can opener, slicer) were observed with an accumulation of food and debris. The food contact surfaces of equipment must be clean to sight and touch. New Violation. Correct By: 03/06/2024

Pasta was observed held at 56 degrees Fahrenheit. Time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food must be held at 41 degrees Fahrenheit or below except during preparation, cooking, or cooling. PIC moved to ice bath. New Violation. Correct By: 03/06/2024

Various foods in the walk-in cooler were observed not marked with the date of preparation. Ready-to-eat time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods prepared in the establishment and held for more than 24 hours must be marked with the date of preparation. New Violation. Correct By: 03/06/2024
Sauce was observed stored on the floor in the kitchen. Food must be stored at least 6 inches above the floor. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 03/06/2024

Inspector observed beverage tubing to be in direct contact with stored ice used for drinks. Beverage tubing installed in contact with ice may result in condensate and drippage contaminating the ice. PIC disposed of ice. Corrected On-Site. New Violation. Correct By: 03/06/2024
Observed an accumulation of frost buildup in the following areas: 1. Freezer (1 door upstairs) 2. Freezer (1 door downstairs) New Violation. Correct By: 03/20/2024
The non-food contact surfaces of the soda gun have an accumulation of black and brown residue. New Violation. Correct By: 03/20/2024

The wall (ledge) in the ware washing area has exposed wood. This material is not durable. Materials for wall surfaces shall be smooth, durable, easily cleanable, and non-absorbent for areas subject to moisture such as food preparation areas, walk-in refrigerators, ware-washing areas, and toilet rooms. New Violation. Correct By: 03/20/2024
